headline: Ordinance on parking and other citation penalties, $20,800,000 bond for Raise project, and PFAS sewer rules.
summary: Other business includes a petition to discontinue part of North Church Street and a $500,000 School Committee request for a snow scraper and vans. Fire Department radio equipment funding, a $10,000 private donation to MPD for a new K9, and commission nominations and confirmations are also listed.
items: Public comment session
Fire Department presentation on public safety radio equipment
Private $10,000 donation to MPD for a new K9
Five pole petitions to be approved under supervision of the Department of Highways
Two residential 50/50 sidewalk petitions: 390 Orange Street and 154 Manning Street
Solicitor's Office report on lawsuits filed against the City
Revolving Loan Fund update
Finance Department reports on receivables and aging
Monthly financial reports (unaudited) for the first month of FY27
Write-off of $344,339.40 in COVID disaster invoices from DPW, Fire, and Police
Ordinance amendment updating Section 70.78 Basic Penalty for parking and other citations
Amended bylaws for the Manchester Arts Commission
Fire Chief request for funding to replace portable radio equipment before December 2026
Tech Freedom Village LLC request to buy five city-owned parcels at Hackett Hill, received and filed
Manchester School District Priority I status and financial report
Resignation of Jessica Margeson from the Housing Commission
Nominations: Jay Brousseau to Highway Commission and Stavros Pliakos to Water Commission, laid over to next meeting
Confirmations: Sam Theodosopolous to Arts Commission, John Clayton to Heritage Commission, Shirley Tomlinson to Ward 6 Board of School Committee
School Committee request to repurpose $500,000 in FY2026 CIP funding for one snow scraper and six 10-passenger vans
Budget projections from Finance Officer Sharon Wickens, if available
Reports of this evening's committees, if available
Final reading of ordinance amending Section 70.78 Basic Penalty
Tabled: petition to discontinue a portion of North Church Street
Tabled: $20,800,000 bond resolution for the 2027 CIP Raise project (DPW-Highway)
Tabled: ordinance amendment on PFAS in Chapter 52 Sewers
plain_text:
BOARD OF MAYOR AND ALDERMEN 
November 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM 
Aldermanic Chambers, City Hall (3rd Floor) 
 
Mayor and All Aldermen 
 
AGENDA 
 
 
The Mayor calls the meeting to order. 
  
The Mayor calls for the Pledge of Allegiance. 
  
A moment of silence is observed. 
  
The Clerk calls the roll. 
  
PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
1. The Mayor advises that the purpose of the public comment session is to give 
residents of Manchester the opportunity to address the Board. All people 
wishing to speak must sign up with their name, address and topic. Once called, 
they will have up to three minutes to speak and any comments must be directed 
to the chair and concluded when their time is up. If the Clerk calls their name 
and they are not present to speak, they will not be given a second opportunity. 
Any resident wishing to speak will come forward to the nearest microphone, 
clearly state their name and address when recognized and give their comments. 
    
PRESENTATION 
  
2. Presentation from the Fire Department regarding public safety radio equipment. 
    
CONSENT AGENDA 
  
Accept BMA Minutes 
  
3. Minutes from the October 20 Finance and BMA meetings.
November 17, 2026 BOARD OF MAYOR AND ALDERMEN 
Page 2 of 5 
 
 
Accept and Remand 
  
4. Private $10,000 donation to MPD for the purchase of a new K9. 
    
Approve Under Supervision of the Department of Highways 
  
5. Pole Petitions: 
• 11-1791, Elm Street (1) 
• 11-1792, 352 Silver Street (1) 
• 11-1794, Garside Way (1) 
• 11-1795, Karatzas Ave (2) 
• 11-1797, Elm Street (1) 
    
Approve Under Supervision of the Department of Highways, subject to funding 
  
6. 50/50 Sidewalk Petitions 
 
Residential: 
• 390 Orange Street 
• 154 Manning Street 
    
Information to be Received and Filed 
  
7. Communication from the Solicitor's Office regarding lawsuits filed against the 
City. 
    
REPORTS OF COMMITTEES 
  
COMMITTEE ON ACCOUNTS, ENROLLMENT AND REVENUE ADMINISTRATION 
  
8. Advising that the update on the City’s Revolving Loan Fund has been accepted. 
(Unanimous vote) 
    
9. Advising that the Finance Department reports: 
• Accounts Receivable over 90 days 
• Aging Report 
• Outstanding Receivables 
have been accepted. 
(Unanimous vote) 
    
10. Advising that the City’s Monthly Financial Reports (unaudited) for the first month 
of FY27 has been accepted. 
(Unanimous vote) 
    
11. Recommending that the request to write-off outstanding invoices related to the 
COVID Disaster Costs incurred by DPW, Fire, and Police in the amount of 
$344,339.40 be approved. 
(Unanimous vote)
November 17, 2026 BOARD OF MAYOR AND ALDERMEN 
Page 3 of 5 
 
 
    
12. Recommending that Ordinance Amendment: 
 
"Amending Section 70.78 Basic Penalty of the Code of Ordinances of the City of 
Manchester to include updated parking and other citations." 
  
ought to pass and be Enrolled. 
(Unanimous vote) 
    
COMMITTEE ON ADMINISTRATION/INFORMATION SYSTEMS 
  
13. Recommending that the amended bylaws for the Manchester Arts Commission 
be approved as presented. 
(Unanimous vote) 
    
COMMITTEE ON COMMUNITY IMPROVEMENT 
  
14. Recommending that the request from the Fire Chief to secure funding for the 
replacement of public safety portable radio equipment before December 
2026 be approved. 
(Unanimous vote) 
(Note: A source for funding was not identified by the Committee.) 
    
COMMITTEE ON LANDS AND BUILDINGS 
  
15. Recommending that the request from Tech Freedom Village LLC to purchase 
five (5) city-owned parcels located at Hackett Hill be received and filed. 
(Unanimous vote) 
    
JOINT SCHOOL BUILDINGS COMMITTEE 
  
16. Recommending that the Manchester School District Priority I status and 
financial report for the period ending September 2026 submitted by LeftField 
has been accepted. 
(Unanimous vote with the exception of Alderman Thomas who was absent) 
    
LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, HAVING READ THE CONSENT AGENDA, A MOTION 
WOULD BE IN ORDER THAT THE CONSENT AGENDA BE APPROVED. 
  
REGULAR BUSINESS 
  
17. Communication from Jessica Margeson advising the Board of her resignation 
from the Housing Commission. 
Ladies and Gentlemen, what is your pleasure?
November 17, 2026 BOARD OF MAYOR AND ALDERMEN 
Page 4 of 5 
 
 
18. Nominations: 
Highway Commission 
Jay Brousseau to succeed Andre Parent as a regular member, term to expire 
January 15, 2029 
Water Commission 
Stavros Pliakos to succeed Craig Brown as a regular member, term to expire 
January 1, 2027 
(Note: Pursuant to Rule 23 of the Board of Mayor and Aldermen, these 
nominations will layover until the next meeting of the Board.) 
    
19. Confirmations: 
Arts Commission 
Sam Theodosopolous to fill a vacancy as an alternate member, term to expire 
December 1, 2028 
Heritage Commission 
John Clayton to succeed himself as a regular member, term to expire 
July 1, 2029 
Ladies and Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
20. Confirmation of Shirley Tomlinson to fill the vacant Ward 6 Board of School 
Committee position, term to expire January 2028. 
Ladies and Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
21. Communication from the Board of School Committee requesting to repurpose 
$500,000 in Fiscal Year 2026 CIP funding to purchase one (1) snow scraper for 
the transportation bus yard and six (6) 10-passenger vans for athletic 
transportation. 
Ladies and Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
22. Budget projections to be submitted by Sharon Wickens, Finance Officer, if 
available. 
(Note: Supporting documentation will be attached to the agenda once it is made 
available to the Office of the City Clerk.) 
    
23. Report(s) of this evening's committees, if available. 
Ladies and Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
24. Ordinance: (A motion is in order to read by title only.) 
 
“Amending Section 70.78 Basic Penalty of the Code of Ordinances of the City of 
Manchester to include updated parking and other citations.” 
This Ordinance, having had its final reading by title only, the question is 
on passing same to be Ordained. 
    
NEW BUSINESS
November 17, 2026 BOARD OF MAYOR AND ALDERMEN 
Page 5 of 5 
 
 
TABLED ITEMS (A motion is in order to remove any item from the table.) 
  
25. Petition to discontinue a portion of North Church Street. 
(Note: Tabled on July 7, 2026.) 
    
26. Bond Resolution: 
  
"Authorizing Bonds, Notes or Lease Purchases in the amount of Twenty Million 
Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars ($20,800,000) for the 2027 CIP C500070327 
Raise - City Funds (DPW-Highway)." 
(Note: Tabled on August 4, 2026.) 
    
27. The Committee on Public Safety, Health & Traffic respectfully recommends, 
after due and careful consideration, that Ordinance Amendment: 
 
“Amending Chapter 52: Sewers of the Code of Ordinances of the City of 
Manchester pertaining to per- and polyfluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS), 
including prohibited discharges, screening, monitoring, control plans, and 
industrial discharge permits.” 
 
ought to pass and be referred to the Committee on Bills on Second Reading for 
technical review. 
(Unanimous vote) 
(Note: Tabled on October 6, 2026.) 
    
ADJOURNMENT
